metadata.summary: Nasser Hussain hailed new England Test captain Joe Root's decision to abolish a team curfew but fears the returning skipper sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader like his predecessor Ben Stokes.
metadata.content: Joe Root: England Test captain right to remove curfew, says Nasser Hussain ahead of three-Test Pakistan series | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Joe Root: England Test captain right to remove curfew, says Nasser Hussain ahead of three-Test Pakistan series Nasser Hussain: "I'm pleased Joe is doing it [Test captaincy], although I may have gone in the direction of Harry Brook"; watch the first Test of the three-match series between England and Pakistan, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10am, Wednesday (first ball 11am) Nasser Hussain Cricket expert and columnist Monday 17 August 2026 06:33, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Test captain Joe Root explains why he has removed the curfew that was previously imposed on his team Nasser Hussain hailed new England Test captain Joe Root's decision to abolish a team curfew but fears the returning skipper sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader like his predecessor Ben Stokes. Root has captained England on a record 65 occasions, most recently during their second Test defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended for breaking a team curfew that was introduced off the back of the 4-1 Ashes defeat in the winter. The Ivorian winger has the potential to be one of the most exciting Premier League arrivals this summer. There were limited opportunities to show that at the World Cup. Toure started only one game. He was introduced in the 89th minute in Cote d'Ivoire's knockout defeat to Norway only after Erling Haaland had scored what turned out to be the winning goal. But Newcastle acted on the evidence of his first full season with Hoffenheim, a wildly impressive campaign in which the club only missed out on Champions League qualification on the final day. metadata.content: F1 title race: Assessing rivals to Kimi Antonelli and factors that will decide 2026 fight ahead of Dutch GP season resumption | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis F1 title race: Assessing rivals to Kimi Antonelli and factors that will decide 2026 fight ahead of Dutch GP season resumption Formula 1 returns from its summer break this week with all still to play for in the fight for the drivers' world title as rivals look to reel in teenage Mercedes star Kimi Antonelli at the summit; watch the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint weekend live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday Monday 17 August 2026 10:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With the Formula 1 season set to resume after the summer break, we look back at how Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli has built a 50-point lead in the drivers' standings Kimi Antonelli is the clear front-runner in Formula 1's 2026 title battle, but which drivers retain a realistic chance of catching him, and what will decide whether a comeback can be successful? Mercedes driver Antonelli, who does not turn 20 until next week, exceeded all expectations to establish a 50-point lead at the top of the standings going into the summer break after the first 11 rounds.
